speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how long it has been since your wisdom tooth extraction and how much bleeding you are currently experiencing? Also, have you noticed any other unusual bleeding or bruising on your body recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any joint swelling or pain in your own knees or elbows after minor bumps, and do you have any family members known to have been diagnosed with hemophilia? Have you experienced any nosebleeds that were difficult to stop or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your family history of joint swelling and bleeding, do you experience deep muscle or joint pain after minor injuries, and have you ever been diagnosed with a clotting disorder? I would also like to review your recent blood work. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Prothrombin Time, Partial Thromboplastin Time, Fibrinogen, and Bleeding Time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37°C (98.6°F), Blood Pressure 108/74 mm Hg, Heart Rate 90/min, Respiratory Rate Normal. Oral Examination: Persistent oozing from wisdom tooth extraction site; no other visible lesions. Skin Examination: Several old bruises of different ages on extremities; no active joint swelling. Hematologic Tests: Hematocrit 35%, Leukocyte Count 8,500/mm3, Platelet Count 160,000/mm3, Prothrombin Time 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time 60 sec, Bleeding Time 6 min, Fibrin Split Products Negative, Peripheral Blood Smear showing normal-sized platelets. Serum Chemistries: Urea Nitrogen 20 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, Total Bilirubin 1.0 mg/d

speaker: Doctor
text: The extended Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT) with a normal Platelet count and Bleeding Time strongly suggests an intrinsic pathway clotting factor deficiency, likely Hemophilia A or B given your family history. To confirm the specific deficiency, I need to check your Factor VIII and Factor IX levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Assay, Factor IX Assay.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Factor VIII and IX levels are normal despite the prolonged PTT, I need to investigate the remaining factors in the intrinsic pathway. Do you have a family history of Von Willebrand disease, and have you ever been told you have high levels of von Willebrand factor or a specific inhibitor? REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen, von Willebrand Factor Activity, Factor XI Assay.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: von Willebrand Factor Antigen: Normal, von Willebrand Factor Activity: Normal, Factor XI Assay: Significantly decreased (consistent with Hemophilia C).

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly decreased Factor XI confirms a diagnosis of Hemophilia C, which aligns with your family history and prolonged PTT. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
